newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end down, break record sequence.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end down, break record sequence.

text.p: Dutch shares ended lower on Thursday, breaking with their recent rally.
"This is just a small pause, due to the dollar, uncertainty about the upcoming U.S. indicators,.... But there are no really big sellers," one dealer said.
Another said Wall Street's drop last night had increased nervousness on the market.
"And there's tomorrow's expiry. That could cause some big index moves," one dealer said.
Dealers were divided upon the market's preferred AEX index level at the time of the option expiry.
The AEX ended 4.52 points lower at 733.71 points, while the midcap AMX lost 15.33 points to close at 1093.76.
Index heavyweight RoyalDutch closed 5.70 lower at 334.80 guilders, pushed down by the dollar and oil prices.
Publishers Elsevier and Wolters Kluwer, two of Wednesday's biggest risers, both had to give up part of their gains as talk on a cooperation between the two and a stock split of WoltersKluwer faded.
"Those rumours come back every now and again, but finally, they don't last," one dealer said.
Elsevier ended down 40 cents at 30.50 guilders, while WoltersKluwer shed 6.40 guilders to 243.50.
Peer publishers VNU and Wegener were among the bourse's risers with VNU up 1.20 at 40.30 guilders and Wegener adding 4.50 to 192 guilders.
"There's definitely something going on in that sector," one dealer said.
ABN Amro was the only financial to close higher, up 1.80 guilders higher at 137.40. Dealers attributed the rise to positive newspaper reports and to speculation on the bank's 1996 results.
KLM closed 1.70 guilders higher at 56.10 guilders.
"We saw some U.S. buying in the share," one dealer said.
Philips lost part of Wednesday's gains as U.S. buyers turned their back to the company.
Both Stork and Fokker shares attracted interest. Shares in the bankrupt plane maker jumped up and down between 1.32 and 3.55 guilders during the day to close down 45 percent at 1.65 guilders.
"Total nonsense what's happening in that stock," one dealer said. Although Fokker shares are not officially listed, they were the sixth heaviest traded shares today.
Stork ended one guilder higher on 74.60 guilders.
Dealers were divided over the direction the Dutch stock market would take on Friday.
"It depends on what the Dow'll do tonight," one said.
"It will be a jojo movement tomorrow because of the expiry," another said.
